title: Keep every Intel Mac on its kernel in the linux-omarchy migration
author: nipunhsud
body:
Fixes #12281.

## Problem

Migration `1789325478` exempts Macs from the `linux-omarchy` swap, but the test only recognises T2 Macs: the `linux-t2` package or a `-t2` kernel release. A T1 or pre-T2 Mac running stock `linux` matches neither, so it is switched to `linux-omarchy` and has `BOOT_ORDER` rewritten. #12097 (MacBookAir6,1 boots to an emergency shell) and #12131 (Haswell Mac HDMI audio underruns) are non-T2 Macs that took that swap.

## Fix

Also skip when `/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor` starts with `Apple`, the same idiom `migrations/1786391100.sh` uses. `OMARCHY_KERNEL_DMI_VENDOR` overrides the path so the test stays hermetic, matching the other `OMARCHY_KERNEL_*` overrides in the file. A missing or unreadable vendor file still migrates, so non-DMI machines and VMs are unaffected.

Machines that already ran the migration are untouched; this reaches late updaters coming from 4.0.3 or earlier.

## Tests

`test/shell.d/omarchy-kernel-migration-test.sh` gains three cases: `Apple Inc.` and `Apple Computer, Inc.` are skipped with no calls, no config change and no marker; a missing vendor file still installs the kernel. All prior cases still pass.

Note: the existing assertion "the superseded migration must not install the PTL variant first" fails on current `quattro` independently of this change, because a73bcbfc re-added `migrations/1789095456.sh` after ff85faf8 removed it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

files.patch:
@@ -1,10 +1,16 @@
 echo "Install the Omarchy kernel and make it the first Limine boot entry"
 
-# linux-omarchy is an x86_64 kernel. T2 Macs must keep their specialized kernel,
-# including when other kernels are installed or the running T2 package is gone.
+# linux-omarchy is an x86_64 kernel. Macs keep the kernel they were installed
+# with: T2 Macs need their specialized kernel, including when other kernels are
+# installed or the running T2 package is gone, and T1 and older Macs carry
+# their own out-of-tree drivers and quirks that linux-omarchy was never tested
+# against (#12097, #12131). Read the DMI vendor for the latter, since nothing
+# else on a pre-T2 Mac names it.
 [[ $(uname -m) == "x86_64" ]] || exit 0
 running_kernel=$(uname -r)
-if omarchy-pkg-present linux-t2 || [[ ${running_kernel,,} == *-t2* ]]; then
+dmi_vendor="${OMARCHY_KERNEL_DMI_VENDOR:-/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor}"
+if omarchy-pkg-present linux-t2 || [[ ${running_kernel,,} == *-t2* ]] ||
+  [[ $(cat "$dmi_vendor" 2>/dev/null) == Apple* ]]; then
   exit 0
 fi

@@ -15,6 +15,7 @@ export INSTALLED_PACKAGES="$scratch/packages"
 export OMARCHY_KERNEL_LIMINE_CONF="$scratch/limine"
 export OMARCHY_KERNEL_LIMINE_DROP_INS="$scratch/drop-ins"
 export OMARCHY_KERNEL_REBUILD_MARKER="$scratch/state/1789325478"
+export OMARCHY_KERNEL_DMI_VENDOR="$scratch/sys_vendor"
 kernel="linux-omarchy"
 boot_order='BOOT_ORDER="linux-omarchy, linux-omarchy-*, *, *fallback, Snapshots"'
 
@@ -82,6 +83,7 @@ reset_fixture() {
   : > "$CALL_LOG"
   printf '%s\n' linux-ptl linux-ptl-headers > "$INSTALLED_PACKAGES"
   rm -f "$OMARCHY_KERNEL_REBUILD_MARKER" "$OMARCHY_KERNEL_LIMINE_DROP_INS/"*
+  printf '%s\n' 'Dell Inc.' > "$OMARCHY_KERNEL_DMI_VENDOR"
   cat > "$OMARCHY_KERNEL_LIMINE_CONF" <<'CONF'
 KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]="root=UUID=keep-me rw cryptdevice=UUID=keep-me:root"
 BOOT_ORDER="*, *fallback, Snapshots"
@@ -133,6 +135,20 @@ TEST_ARCH=aarch64 run_migration
 assert_skipped
 pass "ARM systems cannot receive an x86_64 kernel"
 
+for vendor in 'Apple Inc.' 'Apple Computer, Inc.'; do
+  reset_fixture
+  printf '%s\n' "$vendor" > "$OMARCHY_KERNEL_DMI_VENDOR"
+  run_migration
+  assert_skipped
+done
+pass "T1 and older Macs keep their kernel even without a T2 package or kernel"
+
+reset_fixture
+rm "$OMARCHY_KERNEL_DMI_VENDOR"
+run_migration
+grep -Fxq "$kernel" "$INSTALLED_PACKAGES" || fail "an unreadable DMI vendor is not treated as a Mac"
+pass "machines without DMI vendor information still receive the generic kernel"
+
 reset_fixture
 printf '%s\n' linux-omarchy-ptl-novrr-mm > "$INSTALLED_PACKAGES"
 mkdir -p "$scratch/state" "$scratch/user-markers" "$scratch/omarchy/migrations"

comments.body:
## Recommendation: no blocking issue found in the tested scope

### Verified: Apple machines skip the kernel migration

A/B-tested `33f076aa` against `9c5482c` with simulated package and boot operations:

```text
Apple vendor fixture
  Baseline -> install packages -> change boot configuration
  PR       -> skip migration  -> boot configuration preserved
                                no rebuild marker
```

Both `Apple Inc.` and `Apple Computer, Inc.` are excluded, including a stock-`linux` fixture. Existing T2-package, running-T2 and ARM exclusions remain intact. Non-Apple, missing-DMI and empty-DMI cases still reach the migration path.

**Impact:** prevents pending migrations from switching kernels on these Apple machines. It does not restore machines that already migrated.

### Existing test failure, not introduced by this PR

`omarchy-kernel-migration-test.sh` requires `1789095456.sh` to be absent, but that filename now contains an unrelated Mise repair. The same assertion fails on baseline.

**Suggested follow-up:** correct the stale assertion without deleting the unrelated migration. The untouched full test file is not passing.

**Test scope:** fixture execution only; no Intel Mac boot or real package installation tested.

**Automated AI review:** Astra inspected the PR, Fable 5.1 and a separate Astra session reviewed it independently, then findings were checked against targeted tests.
